text.tspan: The TypeScript Type Space
Think of a type as the SET of values it allows. Unions widen that set; intersections narrow it.
How wide is the set?
any
Every value, and it switches checking OFF. Avoid it.
unknown
Every value too, but you must narrow before using it. The safe any.
string
Every string. A normal, useful type.
'small' | 'large'
Exactly two values. Precise and self-documenting.
never
No value at all. The empty set.
Combining types
Union - A | B - either one
string | number accepts both, so you may only
use what they have in COMMON until you narrow.
Intersection - A & B - both at once
HasId & HasName demands every member of each.
Fewer values qualify, but each has MORE properties.
type or interface?
interface - object shapes you may want to extend.
It can be reopened and merged by a later declaration.
type - everything else: unions, tuples, primitives,
mapped and conditional types. Cannot be reopened.
For a plain object shape either is fine; be consistent.
TypeScript is STRUCTURAL: two types match when their shapes match, whatever they are called; nothing needs to declare
that it implements an interface. And prefer inference: write the annotation where a value ENTERS your code (parameters,
return types, external data) and let TypeScript work out the rest.
